fees.title: UWA - Tuition & Fees (2026-2027 undergraduate costs per semester)

test_policy.notes: First-time freshmen must meet ONE of: ACT 17, SAT 920, or 2.5 cumulative high school GPA, so scores are not strictly required; the page lists ACT/SAT scores as '(if applicable)'. No explicit test-optional statement was found. The international page lists ACT 19 / SAT 980 with the note '(Currently Waived)' and says applicants who cannot test at home take a placement test at UWA on arrival.

requirements.notes: The $30 non-refundable fee is from the domestic undergraduate admissions page (waived during 'It's Free Application Week', Oct. 5-9; no year printed); the international page does not state a fee. International documents: passport valid 6+ months past term start, official high school transcript and diploma (certified translation if not English; a credential evaluation by a NACES or AICE member may be required), English proficiency score, English-language bank statements, sponsor Statement of Financial Support, immunization and medical forms. No minimum bank balance is listed. A $3,000 non-refundable deposit (applied to tuition and fees) is due within 10 business days of visa issuance. No minimum GPA is stated for international applicants.

deadlines.label: International fall application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: International page: documents due Fall Semester June 1, Spring Semester October 1, Summer Semester March 1. The page gives no year, so fall 2027 is assumed. The domestic undergraduate page lists no application deadline.

deadlines.label: Trustee scholarship application deadline
deadlines.notes: Trustee Academic awards range from $2,000 to $12,000 per year (3.0 GPA to renew). April 15 is printed without a year, so 2027 is assumed. Not available to international students attending through a partnership or memorandum of agreement. The international talent and exceptional-student awards list no deadline.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Two tiers: 'Admission' (full) and 'Admission with ESL' (meets the entrance requirement but ESL placement testing and ESL 102/103 coursework may be required after enrollment). Exemptions: secondary or higher degree from an accredited institution in a country where English is the official and primary language of education and government (India/Philippines case by case with a ministry letter); completion of a CEA-accredited English program; a Council of International Schools high school taught in English (ESL placement may still be required); a 'C' or better in Written English I and II at a regionally accredited US institution; undergraduates with high SAT/ACT EBRW scores may petition (no threshold printed). Also accepted: LanguageCert Academic (70 admission / 60 ESL) and TOEIC (770 / 700-769, only under a university agreement). An appeal route exists for scores below the ESL tier (department letter plus support plan, 60 days before the first term).

english.notes: 61-89 = Admission with ESL; 90 = full Admission without ESL.
3.5 = Admission with ESL (matches old 61-89); 4.5 = full Admission (old 90). The page labels these as 2026 scoring.
5.0-6.0 (5.0 minimum on each subscore) = Admission with ESL; 6.5 (6.0 minimum on subscores) = full Admission.

aid.notes: International Talent Scholarship covers in-state tuition plus $100 (about $4,650 per term; 3.0 GPA on transcripts when applying, must live on campus and keep a 3.0 GPA). Exceptional International Student Scholarship is $1,000 per semester for the first two semesters (new students, live on campus, not renewable). Trustee academic awards ($2,000-$12,000 per year) may be open to international students not attending through a partnership agreement. 2026-27 undergraduate costs per 15-credit semester: international tuition $9,750, housing $2,000-$3,600, meal plan $1,752-$2,176, Tiger One fee $1,845 (includes international and student insurance); page total estimate $15,729.50-$17,753.50 per semester.
